findings.problem: The canonical pairing-is-dot-product lemma is not `@[simp]`, although its type A counterpart is. Only the special case `toLinearMap_typeDSimplyConnectedRootDatum_single_single` is `@[simp]`. So `simp` normalizes `toLinearMap (Pi.single i 1) (Pi.single j 1)` but leaves `toLinearMap x y` unreduced for any other `x`, `y`, for example `toLinearMap (root k) (coroot l)` or `toLinearMap v (Pi.single j 1)`. Downstream proofs must pass the lemma by name, as in SpinWeight's `simp [RootPairing.reflection_apply, toLinearMap_typeDSimplyConnectedRootDatum, coroot_typeDSimpleIndex hn]`, or use `rw`, as in GraphAutomorphism's `rw [toLinearMap_typeDSimplyConnectedRootDatum, toLinearMap_typeDSimplyConnectedRootDatum]`. This is the same simplification the A file has built in. The `_single_single` simp lemma is also redundant if the general rule is simp, because `single_dotProduct` and `Pi.single_apply` can then take over.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `toLinearMap_typeDSimplyConnectedRootDatum` as `@[simp]`, as `toLinearMap_typeASimplyConnectedRootDatum` is. The rule rewrites `toLinearMap x y` to `x ⬝ᵥ y` and cannot loop. Then drop `@[simp]` from `toLinearMap_typeDSimplyConnectedRootDatum_single_single`, or keep it as the more specific rule, and remove the explicit lemma from the `simp [...]` call in SpinWeight. I did not run Lean, so the downstream effect on those calls is unchecked.
findings.benefit: The type A and type D pinned data get the same simp interface. `simp` goals that mention the pinned pairing reduce to `⬝ᵥ` on `Fin n → ℤ`, which is where the dot-product simp lemmas apply, without the lemma being named at each use.
